test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 9 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.

As long as there was corruption in India, there can be no progress.
solution:
The correct answer is** "there was corruption"** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** We will here see the grammatical error with the help of the whole sentence:

__
 
• As long as*** there was corruption ***in India, there can be no progress.​
 
• "is" should be used in place of "was"

**Correct sentence**: As long as there **is **corruption in India, there can be no progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Now let's understand the correct sentence formation:

 
• It should be **there is corruption** instead of **there was corruption.**
 
• We use **"is" **in the present tense whereas we use** "was" **in the past tense.
 
• More specifically, we use** "is"** in present continuous tense
 
 
• Eg. He *is* eating food.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, the verb** "was"** is used in past continuous tense
 
 
• Eg. The bird *was *flying to its nest.
